name: Plitvice Lakes National Park
blurb: Beech-fir forest and mossy tufa dams that hold back a chain of lakes.

tip.title: Remove the wolves
tip.text: Wolves and lynx both hunt roe deer. Set Grey wolf to -100% and watch roe deer, then the beech they browse and the ravens that feed on kills.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Plitvice Lakes National Park

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Light reaching the forest floor and the clear lake water drives growth of trees, mosses and algae.
The area gets about 1,500 mm of precipitation a year, which feeds the rivers that form the lakes.
Dominant tree of the park forests, which Wikipedia says cover about three quarters of the area. Its seeds feed dormice, squirrels, voles, deer and bears.
Grows with beech in the old-growth stands of Corkova uvala, where some trees are about 700 years old. Its seeds are food for squirrels.
Browses beech, herbs and shrubs. It is the main prey of the lynx in Europe and a regular prey of wolves.
A common small forest rodent of the park area that eats seeds, fruit and green plants and feeds many predators.

nodes.name: Eurasian red squirrel
nodes.desc: Feeds on tree seeds such as beech nuts and fir seeds.
A scavenger that feeds on carcasses of deer and other animals killed by predators or the winter.
Wikipedia says two native brown trout forms live in the lakes. They feed on aquatic invertebrates.
Hunts fish, frogs and other water animals in rivers and lakes.

nodes.name: Grey wolf
nodes.desc: One of three large carnivores in the park. In Europe it hunts mainly roe deer, red deer and wild boar and also eats carrion.
An omnivore that eats mostly plant food, including beech nuts, plus insects, small mammals and deer, and carrion in spring.
Hunts mainly roe deer in Europe and also hares. May be pushed to smaller prey where wolves are numerous.

story: Plitvice Lakes National Park is one of the oldest and largest national parks in Croatia. Founded in 1949, it covers 296.85 km2 in the mountainous karst area of central Croatia at the border with Bosnia and Herzegovina. The park is famous for its picturesque series of tufa lakes, caves, and connected waterfalls.
matters: The afforested mountain slopes serve as a refuge for many animal species, including the brown bear, grey wolf, and Eurasian lynx. The park is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list for its outstanding natural features.
